title: Green peas, canned, reduced sodium, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Canned green peas are a ready‑to‑eat product made from fresh pea pods that are blanched, drained, and sealed in a reduced‑sodium brine. A vegetable oil is added, but the specific type of fat is not specified (NS). The peas retain their bright green color, natural sweetness, and a slight snap when eaten.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peas are a good source of plant protein and dietary fiber.
Canning extends shelf life to 2–3 years while preserving most nutrients.
Reduced‑sodium brine makes the product suitable for low‑salt diets.
Added fat enhances flavor and improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
Peas belong to the legume family, along with beans, lentils, and soy.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: One cup of canned peas provides about 8 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps regulate blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain vitamin B6, thiamine, and folate, which are important for metabolism.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium, and phosphorus in peas support blood health and bone strength.

items.title: Reduced sodium content
items.content: Lower salt levels make the product more suitable for people monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas.

items.title: Added fat increases calories
items.content: The oil raises the caloric density, so portion control is advised for weight management.

items.title: Sodium still present
items.content: Even reduced, the product contains salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Possible fermentation after opening
items.content: Once opened, store the can in the refrigerator and consume within 3–4 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peas can be eaten cold in salads, added to soups, stews, or pasta dishes. They also heat quickly in the microwave or on the stovetop with a splash of water or broth. Season with herbs, spices, or a squeeze of lemon for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened can in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer leftovers to an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 4 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.
